crossrefs.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,
but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father, who by grace has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope,
encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good word and deed.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,

“I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. To a nation that did not call My name, I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’
We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.
so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another manʼs territory.
The marks of a true apostle—signs, wonders, and miracles—were performed among you with great perseverance.
The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

notes.title: A pure offering in every place

crossrefs.text: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?

I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.

Brothers, although we were torn away from you for a short time (in person, not in heart), our desire to see you face to face was even more intense.
Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for not everyone holds to the faith.

Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.
